prerequisites: Basics of trigonometry, algebra, and calculus: vectors and vector operations, derivatives, integrals, differential equations, coordinate systems.
Basics of physics acquired in the first module (Fisica 1): forces, vector fields, work, energy, power.

learning_outcomes.text: Acquisition of the fundamental concepts of electromagnetism and optics. Understanding of the theoretical principles and physical laws governing electromagnetic and optical phenomena.
Application of concepts and physical laws to the analysis and solution of numerical problems and practical exercises. Ability to connect theory with experimental practice and applied contexts.
Development of critical skills in the interpretation of numerical and theoretical results. Evaluation of the appropriateness of physical models in relation to the problems addressed.

Ability to present theoretical concepts and solution procedures clearly and rigorously, using appropriate scientific language. Ability to argue methodological choices in a logical and coherent manner.
Development of the ability to independently approach the study of more advanced topics in physics. Strengthening of learning capacity through both guided and autonomous problem-solving.

syllabus_topics: Coulomb’s law
Electric field of discrete and continuous charge distributions
Electric flux and Gauss’s law with applications to symmetric charge distributions
Electric potential: definition, relation to the electric field, equipotential surfaces
Electrostatic potential energy and work of electric forces
Conductors in electrostatic equilibrium
Capacitance and capacitors (in series and in parallel)
Energy stored in an electric field
Dielectrics: dielectric constant, polarization, capacitance with dielectrics
Electric current and current density
Resistivity and conductivity; Ohm’s laws
Direct current circuits: resistors in series and parallel, Kirchhoff’s rules
Electric power
Magnetic forces on moving charges and current-carrying conductors
Motion of a charge in a uniform magnetic field (cyclotron motion)
Biot–Savart law
Ampère’s law and applications (solenoid, toroid)
Magnetic moment and magnetic dipoles
Faraday’s law and magnetic flux
Lenz’s law
Inductance and inductors; energy stored in a magnetic field
RL circuits, LC oscillations, and RLC circuits (analogy with mechanical oscillations)
Maxwell’s equations: Integral and differential form
Displacement current
Electromagnetic waves: wave equations, propagation speed, electromagnetic spectrum, energy, and the Poynting vector
Fermat’s principle and Snell’s law of refraction
Reflection and refraction
Thin lenses: conjugate point formulas, magnification
Spherical mirrors
Simple optical instruments: microscope, telescope
Interference: superposition principle, Young’s fringes, thin films
Diffraction: single slit, double slit, diffraction grating
teaching_methods: Collective problem solving in the classroom
assessment_rules: The final examination consists of a written test followed by an oral test. A score of 18/30 or higher in the written part is required to access the oral test. The examination is considered passed if the weighted average of the two components (written and oral) is equal to or greater than 18/30. The result of the written test cannot be retained for a subsequent examination session.
bibliography: D. Halliday, R. Resnick, J. Walker – Principles of Physics -Wiley
